sections.title: Wayfaring tree
sections.text: Viburnum lantana is a deciduous European and western Asian shrub, usually about 3–5 m tall and broad. Its opposite, broadly oval leaves have fine teeth and a conspicuously soft, grey-hairy underside. Flat-topped clusters of small creamy flowers appear in late spring.

sections.title: Fruit
sections.text: The oval drupes change from red to black as they ripen. The botanical plate shows the simple opposite leaves, their grey-hairy undersides, cream flower clusters, and different stages of fruit ripening. The Woodland Trust warns that its fruits are poisonous; no human food use is recommended here.
